title: They Shall Not Grow Old
review: Very good documentary. I haven't seen many of WW1. This did not deal with the causes, battles, strategies, etc, but was very small scale, telling the story at the individual, anonymous soldier's level. No glorification of war. No battle of good and bad. A very healthy war film. Colors and audio histories brought it alive, and took me deeper into the trench reality than other war films have. Impressive that as a documentary, it had similar gruesomeness as the landing in Saving Private Ryan.

The only part where they were asking what's going on was when the film went into abstract thought, and things got a bit psychedelic. I thought it was cool. We watched this in 2D, but I want to watch it in 3D later. It seems well suited for that.

title: Black Panther
review:
Entertaining, but didn't stand out from the rest of the Marvel universe. Much of the same, with different characters. Aside from the entire European-African history being a theme throughout the movie, the film also covered current topics, like immigration and refugees, authoritarianism and problems of a monarchy without a proper system of checks and balances.

My issue with the film is that I felt like it struggled to balance the social and political message with the superhero story, and many plot turns felt forced. Changes in how characters behaved seemed abrupt and unrealistic. After a failed mission, the best friend turns against the king just like that? Without even asking what happened? The villain starts out with a plan to help the oppressed fight back, but is overnight turned into a bloodthirsty tyrant who only cares for power and destruction?

For a modern Marvel superhero movie, special effects seemed mediocre.

As a purely subjective note, the tech utopia of Wakanda looked like an 80s vision of the future with its criss-crossing maglev trains - my hope is that a future city is built more pedestrian friendly...

Despite the critique, I enjoyed watching the movie.

title: Ford v Ferrari
review: Too long. Racing scenes were repetitive and not that exciting. Watching a formula one race is more exciting. Both the original title, Ford v Ferrari and the one used here,  Le Mans 66, are strange choices because the film isn't about either. There seemed to be no rivalry. Just an insecure Ford feeling insulted by Italians. It was possibly meant as a Trump analogy. One problem with the film is that I'm not sure there filmmakers knew what they wanted the film to be about. Main characters' motivations were also left unexplained. If it was all about racing and building a great car, the film proved several times that they should have switched teams, so I'm left to assume it was about money.

title: And Breathe Normally
review: I really liked this film.  I don't know what it is like to be a refugee or a troubled and poor single parent, but the feeling the film conveyed felt realistic. The uncertainty of life as an asylum seeker was demonstrated in small things. Nobody really had answers to her questions - how long until the application is processed, what happens to her next. Not showing the incredibly beautiful nature of Iceland, but concentrating on rain, wind, and greyness was also effective. Beautiful nature might have distracted from the main character's situation. Maybe their situation was also such that they would see even such a beautiful country through a lens of grey hopelessness.
